original_value: SummaryScientists from many different fields have been developing Bulk‐Synchronous MPI applications to simulate and study a wide variety of scientific phenomena. Since failure rates are expected to increase in larger‐scale future HPC systems, providing efficient fault‐tolerance mechanisms for this class of applications is paramount. The global‐restart model has been proposed to decrease the time of failure recovery in Bulk‐Synchronous applications by allowing a fast reinitialization of MPI. However, the current implementations of this model have several drawbacks: they lack efficiency; their scalability have not been shown; and they require the use of the MPI profiling interface, which precludes the use of tools. In this paper, we present EReinit, an implementation of the global‐restart model that addresses these problems. Our key idea and optimization is the co‐design of basic fault‐tolerance mechanisms such as failure detection, notification, and recovery between MPI and the resource manager in contrast to current approaches on which these mechanisms are implemented in MPI only. We demonstrate EReinit in three HPC programs and show that it is up to four times more efficient than existing solutions at 4,096 processes.

result.paraphrase: SummaryScientists across many disciplines have been building Bulk-Synchronous MPI applications to model and investigate a broad range of scientific phenomena. Because larger future HPC systems are expected to suffer higher failure rates, effective fault-tolerance for this application class is essential. The global-restart model was introduced to reduce recovery time in Bulk-Synchronous applications by enabling rapid MPI reinitialization. But existing implementations of this model have several limitations: they are inefficient, their scalability has not been demonstrated, and they depend on the MPI profiling interface, which prevents the use of tools. In this paper, we introduce EReinit, an implementation of the global-restart model that overcomes these issues. Its central idea and optimization is the co-design of core fault-tolerance mechanisms—failure detection, notification, and recovery—between MPI and the resource manager, unlike current approaches where these mechanisms are implemented only in MPI. We validate EReinit on three HPC programs and show that, at 4,096 processes, it is up to four times more efficient than existing solutions.
